title: Common dry-air weights permitted both ozone contrast signs at the 80 ppb target in North Wales on October 1-9, 2021
abstract: We extended an August-September exposure-ranking test into October 1-9 in a 2021 North Wales ozone and warming experiment. A common response between zero and one that decreases with vapor pressure deficit permitted both signs at the 80 ppb peak target. With light above 50 micromoles per square metre per second, exact heated-minus-ambient bounds were -11.861 to +49.049 ppb. A response floor of 0.194729 makes the lower bound zero. In contrast, excess ozone above 40 ppb gave bounds of zero to +26.523 ppb. The earlier August and September bounds were nonpositive. Independent linear programs checked 108 endpoints. The new result concerns response assumptions in a new time window; the unweighted October reversal was already published. October has no flower visits. One site-year, one chamber per combination, shared ambient weather and untested sensor accuracy prevent biological or causal claims. Source records stay external. Code, aggregate evidence and retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Left: weekly recorded concentration contrasts. Right: exact bounds over common non-increasing dry-air responses at the 80 ppb target, using light above 50. The October interval permits both signs. Points show no VPD weight. These are exposure summaries, not uptake or plant effects.
